# Raw frame-length decode ratchet baseline for
# scripts/check-framing-raw-decodes.sh.
# One row per file that still decodes `u32-BE` frame lengths by hand:
#   <count>\t<path>\t<disposition>
# The count is an EXACT ceiling, not an upper bound: the guard refuses a
# count above it (a new hand-rolled copy) AND a count below it (a slice
# landed and nobody tightened the ratchet). Lower the number in the same
# commit as the migration, and delete the row when the file reaches zero.
# Dispositions:
#   pending  — still to migrate onto LengthDelimitedCodec.
#   keep     — deliberate, with the reason recorded in this packet's events
#              AND at the site itself; never silently converted to pending.
# KEEP REASONS, recorded here as well as at each site (795-5itp events
# 2026-08-25T09:47:30Z and the doc comment at vsock_server.rs:1715):
#   headless/src/tray/mod.rs        — the tray control socket is a BLOCKING
#     std::os::unix::net::UnixStream held in an Arc<Mutex<Vec<..>>> subscriber
#     registry and written synchronously inside a retain; Framed needs
#     tokio AsyncRead+AsyncWrite, so this is not a swap but a move of the
#     tray control socket onto a runtime. Its bound is already the shared
#     MAX_MESSAGE_BYTES, so the duplication here is mechanics, not policy.
#     The two test sites are hand-rolled peers of that same socket.
#   headless/src/vsock_server.rs    — #[cfg(test)] interop peer. Its value is
#     being an INDEPENDENT hand-rolled decoder: delete it and "the codec
#     produces the bytes the old framing produced" becomes a tautology.
#   headless/tests/vsock_listener_e2e.rs — same, at the e2e layer.
